lines.text: Twelve people in a room in Washington decide how expensive your mortgage, your car loan and your credit card are going to be.
They set one number: the federal funds rate. Almost every other interest rate moves with it.
In 1980, they pushed it to about 20% to crush inflation.
lines.say: In nineteen eighty, they pushed it to about twenty percent to crush inflation.

events: cut to near zero in the crisis
back to zero in the pandemic

lines.text: In 2008, they cut it to almost zero to rescue the economy.
lines.say: In two thousand and eight, they cut it to almost zero to rescue the economy.
In twenty twenty, back to zero again.

lines.text: And by 2023, it was back up to 5.25 to 5.5%, the highest in over 20 years.
lines.say: And by twenty twenty-three, it was back up to five and a quarter to five and a half percent, the highest in over twenty years.

lines.text: So in this video: how that one number reaches your wallet.
